chapter: Duke, Gensel and the later years
title: The cabaret card: Basin Street East with Duke refused
summary: McGhee could play Basin Street East with Woody but not Duke Ellington's band because of his drug record.

story.theme_name: Duke Ellington and his orchestra, as others knew them
story.community_name: Duke Ellington: the band, the man, his men

blocks.x: Street, and I (?) go in with Duke.
When was this?

This was in '61 or '62, somewhere around there -- maybe '63 even. So we came here to the Apollo, and we played at the Apollo; I was with Duke at the time -- and it was all right. But Duke wanted to go into Basin Street East, and they told me I had to have a cabaret card to play there. So I couldn't get a cabaret card, being that I had been busted in New York. And I had to get somebody to be a champion for me, like Reverend Gensel, you know. He did me a lot of good as far getting my card. But I did him a lot of good by me playing at the Church.
Right, in the early days of him getting started with the Jazz at the Church.
Yeah, well, I was the one that got him hooked up with that church, with the church he's with. So he was the minister up at 93rd and Broadway...
I remember that, because I went to Max Roach and Abby Lincoln's wedding at that church, and he married them.
Yeah.
That's right. I had forgotten about that.
He was up there then. So I wrote a thing for a choir and four trumpets, and we appeared up there at his church and played the music...
McGhee (12/1) - 17
And you recorded for United Artists.
Yeah.
Was this all in the same period?
Yeah. Well shortly after that. This comes after I get through talking about Duke and Woody. Yeah, that's what I was talking about.
I could work at Basin Street East with Woody Herman's band, but I couldn't do it with Duke Ellington's band.
Because of the different sizes of the bands?
No.
Why?
Color.
You could work with Woody in a mixed band...
Yeah, but Duke had a colored band.
...but you couldn't work with Duke's band. Why?
That I couldn't figure out.
That would seem like the opposite of what the usual prejudice was.

Yeah. Now, that's the twister, isn't it? They said, 'You can play with Woody Herman all you want,' and the cabaret man ain't come by or nothin' to even check out whether I had a cabaret card of not. But they minute they heard I was going in with Duke, they told me 'No, you
McGhee (12/1) - 18
can't go in there with Duke."
Yet you were only one man in a big band, and here you were like a feature in a small band.
Yeah. I don't make much sense to me either. I said, "Boy-oh-boy, they throw curves at you all kind of ways." What can you say, you know?
